topics.name: Separation of Mixtures and Purification of Chemical Substances

subtopics.name: Pure and Impure Substances
objectives: Distinguish between pure and impure substances using boiling and melting points.
Differentiate between elements, compounds, and mixtures.
Distinguish between chemical and physical changes.

subtopics.name: Separation Techniques
objectives: Identify appropriate separation methods for different mixtures.
Describe the principles of distillation, filtration, and chromatography.
Explain sublimation, crystallization, and solvent extraction.

subtopics.name: Purification Methods
objectives: Explain criteria for purity of substances.
Describe applications of fractional distillation and column chromatography.
Determine purity using melting and boiling point data.

subtopics.name: Laws of Chemical Combination
objectives: State and apply the law of conservation of mass.
Apply the law of definite proportions in calculations.
Use the law of multiple proportions to identify compounds.

subtopics.name: Mole Concept and Stoichiometry
objectives: Define the mole and calculate molar mass.
Use Avogadro's number in particle calculations.
Perform stoichiometric calculations using mole ratios.
Calculate percentage composition and empirical/molecular formulae.

topics.name: Kinetic Theory of Matter and Gas Laws

subtopics.name: Kinetic Theory and States of Matter
objectives: State the assumptions of the kinetic theory of matter.
Explain properties of solids, liquids, and gases using kinetic theory.
Describe Brownian motion and its significance.

subtopics.name: Gas Laws
objectives: Apply Boyle's law, Charles's law, and the pressure law.
Use Graham's law of diffusion in calculations.
Apply Dalton's law of partial pressures.

subtopics.name: Ideal Gas Equation
objectives: Derive and apply the general gas equation.
Use PV = nRT in calculations.
Distinguish ideal gas behaviour from real gas behaviour.

subtopics.name: Atomic Structure
objectives: Describe the structure of the atom (protons, neutrons, electrons).
Explain atomic number, mass number, and isotopes.
Write electron configurations for elements in the first three periods.

subtopics.name: Types of Chemical Bonding
objectives: Explain ionic, covalent, metallic, and hydrogen bonding.
Describe van der Waals forces and their effects.
Relate bond type to physical properties of substances.

subtopics.name: Molecular Shapes and Intermolecular Forces
objectives: Predict shapes of simple molecules (linear, tetrahedral, pyramidal, bent).
Explain electronegativity and polarity of bonds.
Describe effects of intermolecular forces on physical properties.

subtopics.name: Composition and Properties of Air
objectives: State the percentage composition of air.
Describe methods of separating air components.
Explain rusting and its prevention.

subtopics.name: Water and Its Properties
objectives: Describe the structure and unique properties of water.
Distinguish between hard and soft water.
Explain methods of water purification and treatment.

subtopics.name: Solubility and Solutions
objectives: Define solubility and interpret solubility curves.
Distinguish between saturated, unsaturated, and supersaturated solutions.
Calculate solubility from given data.

subtopics.name: Types and Sources of Pollution
objectives: Identify major air, water, and soil pollutants.
Explain the causes of acid rain and the greenhouse effect.
Describe sources of industrial and domestic pollutants.

subtopics.name: Effects and Control of Pollution
objectives: Describe health and environmental effects of pollutants.
Suggest methods to control air, water, and soil pollution.
Explain the role of legislation in pollution control.

subtopics.name: Acids and Bases
objectives: Compare Arrhenius, Bronsted-Lowry, and Lewis acid-base theories.
Identify properties of acids and bases.
Use indicators and pH to determine acid-base character.

subtopics.name: Salts and Neutralization
objectives: Classify salts as normal, acidic, or basic.
Describe methods of preparing salts.
Perform neutralization calculations using titration data.

subtopics.name: Buffer Solutions and Hydrolysis
objectives: Explain hydrolysis of salts in water.
Describe the action of a buffer solution.
Calculate pH of buffer solutions.

subtopics.name: Oxidation and Reduction Concepts
objectives: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electron transfer and oxidation state.
Identify oxidizing and reducing agents in reactions.
Assign oxidation numbers to elements in compounds.

subtopics.name: Redox Reactions and Balancing
objectives: Construct and balance half-equations for redox reactions.
Identify common redox processes (rusting, bleaching, combustion).
Balance redox equations using the ion-electron method.

subtopics.name: Principles of Electrolysis
objectives: Explain electrolytic conduction in terms of ion movement.
Identify products at electrodes during electrolysis.
Distinguish between electrolytic and electrochemical cells.

subtopics.name: Faraday's Laws and Applications
objectives: State and apply Faraday's first and second laws of electrolysis.
Calculate mass deposited or volume of gas evolved during electrolysis.
Describe industrial applications: electroplating, extraction, and purification.

subtopics.name: Exothermic and Endothermic Reactions
objectives: Distinguish between exothermic and endothermic reactions.
Interpret energy diagrams for chemical reactions.
Explain activation energy and the role of catalysts.

subtopics.name: Enthalpy Changes and Hess Law
objectives: Calculate standard enthalpy changes of combustion, formation, and reaction.
Apply Hess law to calculate unknown enthalpy changes.
Use bond energies to estimate enthalpy changes.

subtopics.name: Factors Affecting Reaction Rates
objectives: Explain how concentration, temperature, surface area, and catalysts affect rate.
Interpret rate-time and concentration-time graphs.
Describe the role of catalysts in industrial processes.

subtopics.name: Collision Theory and Rate Equations
objectives: Explain reaction rate using collision theory.
Define rate constant and order of reaction.
Determine rate from experimental data.

subtopics.name: Dynamic Equilibrium and Le Chatelier Principle
objectives: Define dynamic equilibrium for reversible reactions.
Apply Le Chatelier principle to predict equilibrium shifts.
Explain the effect of temperature, pressure, and concentration on equilibrium.

subtopics.name: Equilibrium Constants
objectives: Write expressions for Kc and Kp.
Calculate equilibrium concentrations from Kc.
Relate equilibrium constant to the position of equilibrium.

subtopics.name: Halogens and Their Compounds
objectives: Describe the properties and reactions of halogens.
Explain the preparation and uses of hydrogen halides.
Describe bleaching and disinfection using chlorine.

subtopics.name: Oxygen, Nitrogen, and Carbon Compounds
objectives: Describe the preparation and properties of oxygen, nitrogen oxides, and ammonia.
Explain the nitrogen cycle and industrial uses of nitrogen compounds.
Describe allotropes of carbon (diamond, graphite, fullerene) and their uses.

subtopics.name: Sulfur and Phosphorus Compounds
objectives: Describe allotropes of sulfur and reactions of sulfur dioxide and sulfuric acid.
Explain the industrial preparation of sulfuric acid (Contact process).
Describe properties and uses of phosphorus compounds.

subtopics.name: Properties and Reactivity of Metals
objectives: Describe general physical and chemical properties of metals.
Use the reactivity series to predict displacement reactions.
Explain the reaction of metals with water, acids, and oxygen.

subtopics.name: Extraction of Metals
objectives: Explain methods of metal extraction (electrolysis, reduction by carbon).
Describe the blast furnace extraction of iron.
Explain the electrolytic extraction of aluminium.

subtopics.name: Metal Compounds and Alloys
objectives: Describe properties and uses of sodium, calcium, and aluminium compounds.
Explain corrosion and its prevention.
Describe common alloys (steel, brass, bronze) and their uses.

subtopics.name: Hydrocarbons
objectives: Name and classify alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes using IUPAC nomenclature.
Describe properties and reactions of alkanes (substitution) and alkenes (addition).
Explain isomerism and homologous series.

subtopics.name: Functional Group Compounds
objectives: Describe the properties and reactions of alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, and carboxylic acids.
Explain esterification and saponification reactions.
Identify functional groups from chemical tests.

subtopics.name: Reactions of Organic Compounds
objectives: Describe addition, substitution, elimination, and condensation reactions.
Explain fermentation and its industrial applications.
Describe the cracking of petroleum fractions.

subtopics.name: Polymers and Industrial Organic Chemistry
objectives: Distinguish between addition and condensation polymers.
Give examples and uses of natural and synthetic polymers.
Describe fractional distillation of crude oil and uses of fractions.

subtopics.name: Industrial Processes
objectives: Describe the Haber process for ammonia production and its conditions.
Explain the Contact process for sulfuric acid production.
Describe the Solvay process for sodium carbonate.

subtopics.name: Petroleum and Its Products
objectives: Describe fractional distillation of petroleum and uses of fractions.
Explain cracking and reforming of hydrocarbons.
Describe environmental impacts of petroleum use.

subtopics.name: Biotechnology and Fertilizers
objectives: Explain the role of microorganisms in industrial processes.
Describe the production and uses of fertilizers.
Discuss the environmental impact of fertilizer use.
